Keywords: attention interest desire action hook persuade engage convert
Description: The most timeless copywriting formula. Captures attention, builds interest, creates desire, and drives action.
Best For: Email campaigns, sales pages, ads, landing pages
Example: Attention: Tired of losing leads? Interest: Most businesses waste 60% of their ad budget. Desire: Our system recovers lost leads automatically. Action: Start your free trial today.
Do: Open with a bold stat, question, or provocative statement. Build emotional desire before logic. One clear CTA.
Dont: Don't start with your company name. Don't skip the desire phase. Don't have multiple CTAs.
CTA Examples: Start Free Trial, Get Instant Access, Claim Your Spot

Keywords: problem agitate solution pain point frustration fix resolve
Description: Identifies the reader's problem, amplifies the pain to create urgency, then offers the solution.
Best For: Short-form ads, landing page intros, email hooks, social posts
Example: Problem: Your email open rates are dying. Agitate: Every day you delay, competitors steal your customers. Solution: ProMail's AI subject lines double opens in 30 days.
Do: Name the exact problem your audience feels. Use emotional language in Agitate. Present solution as inevitable relief.
Dont: Don't agitate without a solution. Don't be vague about the problem. Don't use generic pain points.
CTA Examples: Fix This Now, Stop the Bleeding Today, See the Solution

Keywords: before after bridge transformation result outcome vision
Description: Shows the contrast between where they are (before) and where they could be (after), then bridges the gap.
Best For: Testimonials, social proof, service pages, case studies
Example: Before: Spending 10 hrs/week on manual reports. After: Our clients spend 30 minutes. Bridge: Reportly automates your entire reporting workflow.
Do: Paint a vivid before picture they recognize. Make the 'after' aspirational but believable. Bridge should feel easy.
Dont: Don't make 'before' too negative. Don't make 'after' sound unrealistic. Don't skip the bridge.
CTA Examples: See How It Works, Get to Your After Today, Make the Switch

Keywords: promise proof proposal problem credibility trust evidence
Description: Structure that covers Problem, Promise, Proof, and Proposal — covers all buying objections.
Best For: Sales pages, long-form copy, product launches
Example: Problem: Leads ghost you after demos. Promise: Never lose a warm lead again. Proof: 2,300 companies recovered 41% more deals. Proposal: Get RecoverLeads free for 14 days.
Do: Use real stats for Proof. Make the Proposal feel low-risk. Address the most painful problem first.
Dont: Don't use vague promises. Don't skip social proof. Don't make the proposal complex.
CTA Examples: Claim Your Free Trial, Get Proof + Access, Start Recovering Leads

Keywords: story character guide plan success failure brand narrative
Description: Positions your customer as the hero and your brand as the guide. Creates an emotional narrative that resonates.
Formula: Character (Customer) → Problem → Guide (You) → Plan → Call to Action → Avoid Failure → Success
Best For: Brand messaging, websites, about pages, pitch decks
Example: Character: Small business owners drowning in tasks. Problem: Tools are complex. Guide: We built it simpler. Plan: Install → Connect → Automate. CTA: Try Free. Avoid: Wasted hours. Success: Run your business effortlessly.
Do: Always make the CUSTOMER the hero. Position your brand as Yoda, not Luke. Be explicit about what failure looks like.
Dont: Don't make your brand the hero. Don't skip the failure consequence. Don't have unclear success outcomes.
CTA Examples: Become the Hero, Start Your Story, Guide Me There

Keywords: features advantages benefits value proposition why it matters
Description: Translates features into benefits. Connects what the product does to why the customer should care.
Best For: Product pages, demo scripts, sales calls, comparison pages
Example: Feature: 256-bit encryption. Advantage: Military-grade security. Benefit: Sleep soundly knowing your data is safe.
Do: Always end on the benefit (the emotional win). Use FAB for every key feature. Focus on 'so what does this mean for you?'
Dont: Don't list features without benefits. Don't over-explain advantages. Don't use jargon.
CTA Examples: Protect What Matters, Feel Secure Today, Experience the Difference

Keywords: problem amplify story testimony offer response pastor framework
Description: Extended PAS with Story, Testimony, Offer, and Response — great for long-form persuasion.
Formula: Problem → Amplify → Story → Testimony → Offer → Response
Best For: Sales pages, webinar scripts, long-form email sequences
Example: Problem: Agencies waste 15hrs/week on reporting. Amplify: That's $3,000/month gone. Story: Our founder faced this. Testimony: 'Saved us 12hrs/week' - CEO. Offer: Agency Suite $299/mo. Response: Start free.
Do: Use real customer stories in the Story phase. Include specific, named testimonials. Make the offer irresistible.
Dont: Don't rush past the story. Don't use fake or vague testimonials. Don't bury the offer.
CTA Examples: Claim the Offer, Join 500+ Agencies, See My Results

Keywords: value prop unique selling proposition USP differentiation why us why you
Description: Clearly communicates who you serve, what you do, and why you're different — usually in one sentence.
Do: Homepage hero, ads headlines, elevator pitch, sales deck
Dont: For SaaS founders who struggle with churn, ChurnZero is a retention platform that predicts and prevents cancellations. Unlike generic analytics, we give you AI-driven playbooks per account.
CTA Examples: Be specific about the target. Use a real differentiator (not 'better quality'). Test multiple versions.
Tone: Don't be vague about who it's for. Don't use 'world's best' claims. Don't ignore the alternative.
column12: Learn Why We're Different, See the Proof, Compare Us

Keywords: spin situation problem implication need payoff sales discovery questions
Description: Question-based framework for consultative selling. Uncovers pain and creates urgency through structured questions.
Best For: Sales calls, discovery emails, chatbots, demo requests
Example: Situation: How do you currently track leads? Problem: Where do leads fall through the cracks? Implication: What does that cost per lost deal? Need-Payoff: How would automated follow-up change your close rate?
Do: Ask one type of question at a time. Let the prospect do 70% of talking. Lead to Need-Payoff naturally.
Dont: Don't skip Situation questions. Don't ask multiple Implication questions too fast. Don't pitch before Need-Payoff.
CTA Examples: Book a Discovery Call, See Your Solution, Let's Map Your Pain Points

Keywords: headline title hook clickbait subject line curiosity gap promise number
Description: Proven formulas for headlines that get clicks, opens, and attention.
Formula: How to [Achieve Goal] Without [Pain] / [Number] Ways to [Result] / The Secret to [Desired Outcome] / Warning: [Bold Statement]
Best For: Blog titles, email subjects, ad headlines, landing page H1
Example: How to Double Your Revenue Without Hiring / 7 Email Subject Lines That Doubled Opens / The Secret to Closing 40% More Deals / Warning: Your Landing Page Is Losing You 63% of Leads
Do: Use specific numbers. Create curiosity gaps. Promise a clear benefit. Test 3-5 headlines before publishing.
Dont: Don't use clickbait with no delivery. Don't be vague. Don't make it about your company.
CTA Examples: Learn the Secret, See the Full List, Get the Framework
